activities.title: Make Comparisons
activities.content:
Compare Illustrations
• Show pupils how to open their Pupil Books to the 
first page. Hold up the Pupil Book so that pupils 
can see the page for Lesson 1 and point to the first 
illustration.
• Say: An dorome londi naatali hana ke wure xo kundu. 
Mani daaba siiha ni ke yi?  Iyo Na ñani.
• Point to the next picture in the row, to the right of the bull. 
• Say: na o dorommu ñoomi natali hana ke yi. Ma a do kebe ga riini I su ni banen ya yi ba? Haani!"
• Point to the next picture in the row. 
• Say: O na ho tana haayi. Ma a do ho hana ken xawa ba? Haani!"
• Point to the final picture in the row. 
• Say: Ma ke do natali hana ken Xawa ba? I yo.
• Continue this process with the other rows, each time asking the pupils to study the first 
illustration and find the other illustration in the row that matches.
 Compare shapes
• Ask pupils to turn to the next page in the Pupil Book.
• Use the same process as the activity above with the shapes on the next page of the Pupil Book.

activities.title: Story sequence
activities.content:
Tell a story using pictures
• Show the next page in the Pupil Book.
• Say: An kitti dooromme sagundi nataali hana ke wure. A  kaman na mani daba riini?"
• Call on two pupils to respond.
• Talk with pupils about each picture in the sequence (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6). Ask pupils what the 
people are doing in each picture and ask questions to help them think about the pictures.
• Ask pupils to look at the pictures and describe the story the pictures are telling. Help them see 
that the woman is preparing "banku".

activities.title: Trace lines
activities.content:
Follow lines with a finger
• Show the next page in the Pupil Book.
• Say: Yaxanbaane ken a mani daba riini natali .ke di? O na deema a nan katu xooda ki rondini  
jalan di. O pare ya ba? An kitte dorome wutu na killen ke koyi xooda ke ga telle dingira be.
• Show pupils how to trace the line from the ball to the goal with a finger.
• Say: Hununxulle ke ma mani daba riini? Xa simmaye maxa a lahini mani ya?
• Watch as pupils trace the line from the monkey to the banana with a finger.
• Repeat with the remaining image.

sessions.title: Session B
learning_outcomes: Recognize the front cover, back cover, and title of a book.
Apply new words learned to own life and use new words in conversation.
Use background knowledge to build meaning.
Use verbal and nonverbal communication appropriately.

activities.title: Parts of a Book
activities.content:
Recognize the Grade parts of a book - cover, 
back, title
• Point to the cover and back of a book.
• Say: We are going to read from the front to the 
back.  
• Say: The words at the front of the page tells you the title of the page book. The title tells you 
what we will read about.
• Say: "When we reach the end of the story, we will see the back of the book." 
• This is the front page of the book.
• Point to the cover and back of a book.
• Say: O na xaranŋen joppana nan bogu kaane kata halle. Ke ya ni bukki ke kaane dingira hana 
ŋa.
• Say: Diganxannu ku be nu ga bukki dere ke kaane kamma, ku ñan bukki ke digañimmu ku yi . 
Diganñimmu ku ya a koyini o da o ga hibe xaranŋa 
• Say: Waxati be o ga na kiñe gumanŋe ke ñemeraŋa, O na bukki ke halle walla.

activities.title: Vocabulary – before reading
activities.content:
Teach and discuss vocabulary
• Tell pupils each word. Have them repeat it but do not write it on the board. Ask pupils what 
they know about each one.
• Discuss the word meaning, using gestures or illustrations to support understanding. If 
needed, help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they know.
buccine, gaadine gida

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
Read the following story aloud 
• Use the appropriate big book or supplementary illustrations if available
• While reading, pause to think aloud and talk to pupils about the story at key moments such as 
when you come to a vocabulary word the pupils just learned.
Faatu buccinen ni
Faatu ma ñaxali. A ma ñi hoo ho dada riinii ka ke di. A di I bayi wari ke gani bintu a wa yillen gollo.  
Bayi n lawayi an deemana ba? "Ee haani, Faatu, an ŋa hi gabe xaraŋa buru!" Keta Faatu daga na 
laato.
A da I kamanne  wari a wa i kande  ke saxundine do me batte ŋa  moxo siri. N gida ñaxare, mi 
lawayi an deemana ba? "Ee haani, Faatu, an ŋa  xarana buru. Keta Faatu daga na laato. 
. Ketaa yaxare  ke da I gida yugon wari a wa soxono gaadinen noxondi ,N Gida yugo n lawayi an 
deemana ba? "Ee haani, Faatu, an ŋa hi gabe xarana buru. Keta Faatu daga na laato.
a di i gida ñaxare ŋari xadi, a wa i xaran gollu daba riini. N gida ñaxare n lawayi an deemana ba? 
"Ee haani, Faatu, an ŋa hi gabe xarana buru.
" ken noxondi, a daga i haaban bange. A haaba da a trindi. N xana Faatu,  mani ña an ga ma 
ñaxali?
N wa hi gabe  xarana, ŋa na yillen gollu. " ŋa hi gabe  xarana, ŋa na kandun moxo sirondini. . " ŋa 
hi gabe  xarana, ŋa na yi soxono gadinen di a do ŋa hi gabe  xarana, ŋa na i xaran gollu daba riini. 
N lawayi mani daba riini? 
Yaxare ke  haaba ti,  "Ee Faatu,! maxa butu an xooro moxon siren ni, n lahi sere ya  yi, kebe kitten 
gadin deema, nin leemunu ku moxon sirondi nda. An lawayi n deemana ba? A da deema.

activities.title: Rapid review
activities.content:
Review the parts of a book - cover, back, title
• Call on a volunteer pupil to show the class which part of a book you start reading from. Ask 
what this part of the book it is called. (correct response: ("front page")
• Say: An da gumanŋe ke toxon kita minna ?   
• (correct response: (bukki kaane saxikamma)  ( buuki taxaade kamma)
• Call on a volunteer pupil to answer. Call on a second volunteer pupil to say the title of the 
story that was just read aloud.
• Say: O ga na kiñe bukkin ñemiranŋa, o na mani walla?  
• (correct response: bukki halle saxikamma )
• Call on a volunteer pupil to answer and point to the back of the book.Language-Less

sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Track objects from left to right with their eyes, and wi.th a finger.
Recognize details in letter shapes as being similar or different from each other
Follow lines with their finger.

activities.title: Make Comparisons
activities.content:
Compare shapes of capital letters  
• Hold up the Pupil Book so that pupils can see the 
page and point to the first capital letter. Do not say 
the name of the letter - this is NOT an activity for 
pupils to learn letters. It is an activity for pupils to 
practice telling the difference between letter and 
shapes. 
• Say: N haayi doromu wutu na ñoomi aigiri hanna ŋa. Seren maxi I doromum wutu na ñoomi. O 
haayi riini hoo tana  muuru hebe ga xo ke moxo.
• Point to the next one in the row.
• Say: O na o doromu lo  xotte hanna ke kamma.A do ho hana ke su baana ba? Haani!
• Point to the next one in the row.
• Say: O na xotte tana haayi ma a do hoo hana ke baane.
• Point to the final one in the row.
• Say: maa ke  do hoo hana ken baane ya ba? I yo!
• Continue this process with the other rows, each time asking the pupils to study the first 
capital letter and find the other one in the row that matches it.
Compare shapes
• Use the same process as the activity above with the small letters on the next page of the Pupil 
Book. Do not say the name of the letter - this is NOT an activity for pupils to learn letters. It is 
an activity for pupils to practice telling the difference between letter shapes.

activities.title: Describe differences
activities.content:
Talk about the differences between objects
• Hold up the Pupil Book so that pupils can see the four objects in the next activity. Ask pupils to 
point to the objects in their own books.
• Call on pupils to describe what images go together and why (there is no 1 correct answer).

activities.title: Trace lines
activities.content:
Follow lines with a finger
• Say: O na a wara do ku huuñu. Ho hana ken ni xerelenŋe ñayi. O na o dooromme loo 
joppandira ke  yi. A do o na  wara da a ga bontene moxo be. 
• Demonstrate following the line on the page as needed.
• Repeat with the remaining images.

sessions.title: Session B
learning_outcomes: Know that words are separated by spaces.
Use new words correctly in sentences.
Answer factual questions.
Use verbal and non-verbal communication appropriately.

activities.title: Words are separated by spaces
activities.content:
Describe what a word is, and why there are 
spaces between them
• Take out the read aloud book from yesterday's 
lesson.
• Choose a sentence to write on the board. 
• Say: This sentence comes from the story that I . We will talk about spaces that are found in 
words. read to you. 
• In a sentence. When I read, I read each word one by one, because every word has a 
meaning.
• Say: Ke digantaa giri  gumanŋe keban ga da a xara xa da.
• O wa digaamunu biran dooru kamma ku be nu ga diganxannu noxondi.
• Digantaa noxon dii.Ŋa na xara, ŋa digaamu ku xaran  na baane baane, boyinu  digaame su da 
wuren ña keta.
• Point to a word in the sentence. Read the word and say its meaning.
• Point to the space after the word.
• Say: Bira ke be ga diganxannu naxa ke ña na koyini ŋa diganxannen ga sikki dingira beyi a do a 
ga joppene xa di dingira be yi.
• Point to the following word in the sentence. Read the word and say its meaning.
• Say: Bira ke be ga diganxannu naxa, A wa an  deemana nan katu hon xaraŋa na. An gana 
digantaa siya gabe saha kubeenu ganta baana, an ga lahi ni na xottu ku rondi bera buro ku 
naxa.

• Write another sentence. Choose a volunteer to help demonstrate on the new sentence.
• Say: An dooromme londi digaxanne ke wuru. Saasa, digaxanne tana koyi An lawa koyinin ŋa 
kan moxo nanti ku digaxannu hilli nta baana?
• (correct response: Bira dooru ke be gi naxa ŋa.)
• Pick up the book. Walk around the room. Ask 3 pupils to find a space between two words, and 
put their fingers on it.

activities.title: Read sight words
activities.content:
Learn two new sight words
• Point to the pictures of the boy and girl in the Pupil 
Book.
• Say: Ke ni Abu, Ke ni Faatu. O wa hi gabe ya xaran 
¿a  I kamma ke waxati di.
• Say: An kitti dorome lo Abu toxon wure, An kitti 
dorome lo Faatu toxon wure.
• Point to the following activity in the Pupil Book (matching activity).
• Ask pupils to point to [BOY NAME] Abu on the left side, then point to the matching name on the 
right side. Repeat with [GIRL NAME]. Faatu
• Point to the following activity in the Pupil Book (box with boy and girl names).
• Ask pupils to say the first name in the left column, then point to the matching name in the row.
• Continue in the same way with each row.•

activities.title: Read a sentence
activities.content:
Read a sentence using sight words
• Say: N da Faatu wari sahene bukki dere ke kamma. Nda diganxanne Kurumba wari sasa, ke 
digan Kurumba ti Bawoni o da yaxane ke toxon tu a do digan Kurunba ke, o rawayi nataali ke 
xarana na a gahibe kono.
• Point to the first picture sentence on the page in the Pupil Book. Ask pupils to name the 
picture on the right.
• Read the picture sentence aloud to pupils, showing them how you point to the pictures/word 
with your finger as you read.
• Continue to the next picture sentence. Ask pupils to point to the boy.

• Point to pictures or words as you read. [BOY NAME sees a goat].  Aba da sugo ŋari.
• Remind pupils that korosinde means "to observe" or "to see."
• Make a gesture to demonstrate seeing. Then, ask pupils to read the picture sentence again 
together.
• Say: Sasa an da ko wari wureeda ke? O na on kittun saxu digantaa ke kamma o na digantaa ke 
xara doome Faatu da taabali wari.
• Say: Ko rawayi digantaa ke xaranŋa ke be ga dawara do a yi?
• Continue calling on pupils to read the picture sentences until the end of the page.

activities.title: Describe differences
activities.content:
Talk about the differences between objects 
Point to the next activity in the Pupil Book.
• Say: O na o kittun doromun taaxu natali hana ke wure. Xada mani wari? Ma xa da xorondame 
wari ke be ga riini riini xadi ba?
• Point to the next picture in the row.
• Say: Iyo Na ña ni! Man  da Na do Jaxen bogu me wure.
• Continue with other illustrations.

activities.title: Draw shapes
activities.content:
Practice drawing common shapes
• Ask pupils to trace each shape in the Pupil Book with one finger.
• Ask pupils to try to draw 3 of each shape in their exercise books. Depending on their comfort 
with writing and drawing, different pupils may focus on just one shape or draw many.

activities.title: How to read – track with a finger
activities.content:
Teach how to track words with a finger
• Say: N ga na xara, N wadigaamu ku xaranŋa na 
baane bane , boyinu  digaamu su da wuren keta. 
An xatu a haamunu an ŋa hibe xarana , nahan wa a 
di siri nan katu xotte su xara. An kittin dooromme 
saxundi xotte su wure an ga na yi xarana a wa an 
deemana an ga nta bontene xotte yi moxo be."
• Write a sentence on the board. Demonstrate how to track with your finger under each word as 
you read. Be sure to place and pause your finger under the specific word.
• Call on a pupil at random to describe what to do with a finger while reading.
• Call on 2 pupils to demonstrate tracking words of the sentence on the board while you read it 
aloud.

activities.title: Vocabulary – before reading
activities.content:
Teach and discuss vocabulary
• Tell pupils each word. Have them repeat it but do not write it on the board. Ask pupils what they

• Discuss the word meaning, using gestures or illustrations to support understanding. If needed,

Faatu, gollo,  deemande.

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
Reread the following story aloud 
• Use the appropriate big book or  supplementary illustrations if available
• Partway through the story, pause to show pupils how you track reading with your finger below 
each word you read as you read it. At the end of the line of text, make a big sweeping motion 
back to the start of the next line of text. Continue tracking with your finger.
• After demonstrating, complete the read aloud.

activities.title: Vocabulary – after reading
activities.content:
Check for vocabulary understanding
• Ask pupils if they heard the new vocabulary words during the read aloud.
• Call on 3-4 pupils to say what vocabulary word they heard and to say the meaning in their own 
words.
• Say: Sasa o na diganxannu ku wutu o ga da hi be xara na diganta dabari
• Give an example by using one of the words in a new sentence - one that is not in the pupil 
book or read aloud.
• For each other vocabulary word introduced before reading, ask a pupil to use the word in a 
new sentence. Have pupils act out a word, if appropriate. Congratulate, help, or correct the 
pupils, depending on the responses.

activities.title: Rapid review
activities.content:
Review tracking words with a finger
• Ask a volunteer pupil to tell you something you should do to be sure you don't skip words while 
reading. (Correct response - track the words with your finger, or follow under the words with 
your finger, etc.)
• Ask one pupil to demonstrate tracking for the class using the book.

activities.title: Comprehension questions— factual
activities.content:
Review the question word "Who" (" KON ")
Read the question: 
• Say: Kon da Jarandaana ke xiri waxatin be Adama ga tooyi?
• Answer: Adama haaba yan da jaarandaa ke xiri,Waxatin be Adama ga toyi?
• Ask pupils to answer the question. Give them feedback. 
• Ask pupils if they can tell you what the question word "ay" is asking about. Call on one or two 
pupils to respond. Let them know if they are correct, or incorrect and why. (Response: the 
question word  "ay" asks us the name of a someone or something alive)
• Teach pupils to use the question word  ("bóbey")
• Tell pupils that they will learn a new question word today, ("bóbey") Tell pupils that they will 
use it to answer the next question.
• Read the question: 
• Say: A gana toyi, an dagana mina?
• Say: Diganqanne ki be gani 'Minna', a na o tirindini dingira ñayi ma ñan moxo. N ga na 'Minna' 
mugu, ŋa a tunu nan ti jaabinde ke ñaana dingira ñayi.
• Read the question: 
• Say: Adama ñi mina biran be a ma do haaba ga ñi a gangunu? Jaabinde: (Adama ñi I kompne ya 
di waxatin be a haaba  do a ma ga ñi a gangunu.
• Say: O na o simmayun deŋe kata  o ga da dingira ke be xara . Guman ŋe ke ti: a wa hinna saxa 
baren kamma.
• Ask pupils to think about "where", or the place, that this happened.
• Call on pupils at random to respond.
• Read the question: 
• Adama haaba da sirimen sanke ke xobo mina yi?
• Answer: Jaabinde: Adam haaba da sirimen sanke ke xobo marasen di.
• Turn and Talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to talk about their answers to the 
question. Remind pupils that it is a  "Minna" question.
• Call on a pupil to share their answer. Ask the rest of the class if they agree.

sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Display mastery of key skills learned over the last four lessons: the parts of a book, spaces between words and tracking a finger under print.

activities.title: Assessment
activities.content:
Special assessment - assess week 1 skills:
1. Know what the "cover " and "back " of the 
book means.
2. Understand that words in print are separated by 
spaces.
3. Know that tracking a finger under a word helps 
keep track of where you are reading.
1. Know what the "cover" and "back" of the book means.
• Hand out pupil books
• Tell pupils to hold up their books and point to the "front". Give feedback and explain. Give more 
examples if needed. If you see any pupil struggling, make sure to support them in this skill during 
the next lessons.
• Tell pupils to hold up their books and point to the "back" of the book. Give feedback, and explain 
and give more examples if needed.
2. Understand that words in print are separated by spaces
• Ask pupils to turn to the first decodable story in their book. Show them the picture for the story, 
so they can find the story in the book. They will not be able to read this story yet, but that is 
alright. Do not ask them to read the story.
• Point to the "space" between the first two words in the story. Ask all pupils to put their finger on 
that space. Walk around and show them where to put their finger.
• Ask pupils to point to the next space in the story. Walk around to observe and give feedback.
• Ask pupils to raise their hand if they know what that space is for (why it's there). 
• Ask a volunteer to answer. Ask another pupil if the response is correct.
• Say: Bera kebe gi  naxa , ken haayi a koyini nan ti diganxannu ku nta baane.
3. Know that tracking a finger under a word helps keep track of where you are reading
• Open a big book (any big book) to the first page. Ask pupils to watch and listen. Read the first 
sentence while pointing to (tracking) each word with your finger.
• Ask pupils what you were doing with your finger. Then ask them why you did that. Tell the pupil 
who responds if they are correct or not. Then repeat or say the correct response. (Possible 
response: I was tracking a finger under the words as I read them. Tracking with a finger helps 
you know where you are while reading, so you don't get confused or lost.)

activities.title: Reinforcement Activity
activities.content:
NOTE
• Look at the list of key skills below. Choose one that your pupils need to practice. Ask pupils to 
turn back to that page in the Pupil Book and repeat that activity.
Key activities from week 1 lessons
1. Draw lines and shapes
2. Read sentences with sight words
3. Choose the letter that matches the first letter in the row
4. Recognize sight words (character names)

sessions.title: Session B
learning_outcomes: Tell a story using pictures.
Recognize sight words, and read them in a sentence.
Track words from left to right with their eyes and with a finger.

activities.title: Story sequence
activities.content:
Tell a story using pictures
• Point to the picture story in the Pupil Book.
• Say: Place your finger under the first picture. What 
is the person doing?
• Call on two pupils to respond.
• Talk with pupils about each picture in the sequence 
(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6). Ask pupils what the people are 
doing in each picture and ask questions to help 
them think about the pictures.
• Point to the picture story in the Pupil Book.
• Say: An kittin doromme saxundi natali hana ke wure. Sere ke na mani daba riini?
• Ask pupils to look at the pictures and describe the story the pictures are telling.

activities.title: Read a sentence using sight words
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to independently read the picture sentences using the sight words they learned 
yesterday. Walk around the room to monitor and help pupils as needed. Ensure that pupils are 
reading from left to right and tracking the pictures/words with their finger.
• After giving pupils an opportunity to read the sentences, call on pupils at random to read aloud 
the first 6 picture sentences.

sessions.title: Session A
learning_outcomes: Identify and say the target vowel sound and recognize the letter that represents that sound.
Hear and recognize in writing the difference between the short and long vowel sound.
Write the letter.

activities.title: Letter and keyword
activities.content:
Teach the Letter
• Point to the lowercase letter /a/ on the alphabet 
poster or on the board.
• Say: ke yani o xotti kuruban ŋa lenki. Xotte ke sehe 
xannen ni/a/. O na ko doome:/a/
• Point to the lowercase letter /a/ on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Harisa xotti baanane ke ya ni hi be sehe xannen gani /a/. A gana digantan joppa ma toxo, o 
na walla sahene kundu ya yi /A/
• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).
• Point to the uppercase letter "a" on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: Waxati gabe , o na a walla sahe ni diganxotte noxondi kundu ya yi.
• Point to the lowercase letter "a" on the alphabet poster or on the board again.
• Say: Ke xotte 'a' ni sigiri xotten sehexanne dambe yogo ña ni. O wa sigiri xotti gabe sehexannu 
xaranŋa na koyi riyi. Asiren ya yi, o na o sigiru sehexannu tu, bawoni o wa i walla diganqanne di 
o ga hibeenu xaranŋa na.

activities.title: Teach pupils to hear syllables
activities.content:
Clap two-syllable words
Say: An rawayi diganxotte borotono gudanun ŋa. Guda su da sigirin xotten kita a noxondi ya. Xo o 
gada xara moxon  ka/ba/ . O sooxo o na a haayi. 
Model by clapping:  → /ka/ 
• Practice together with pupils:  
• WORD  → SYLLABLES /barama/ ba ra ma /,  WORD → SYLLABLES Pupils practice alone: 
• WORD  → SYLLABLES /kaba/ ka ba /, WORD → SYLLABLES  / bafa/  ba fa/  
• Clap words with different numbers of syllables
• Say: Ku diganxottun da gudampillo ya kita, bari diganxotte rawayi guda baane, gudan sikko kittana 
maa hi be gan pongu ken ŋa. O na diganxottu yogo nu seera ba. Npayi diganxotte ke konno. Sasa 
on suu sooxo doome taanu hilli.  
ba/  ja /baja      /ja/ fa/ ra/jafara

activities.title: Short and long vowel sound
activities.content:
Hear and see the short vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture on the page of the Pupil Book.
• Say: An da mani wari?
• Ask one pupil to name what is in the picture. Repeat the correct word. If needed, help pupils 
understand the word by saying it in another language they know.
• Say: O na sooxo gudanu ku yi diganxotte ku noxondi. (daga ,da ga)  An da /a/ sehexanne mugu 
taanu manime diganxotten (daga) di? On sooxo xadi.
• Touch the letter in the Pupil Book. Say the sound. If pupils struggle to hear and say the sound, 
help them by saying another word with that sound in your language or another language they 
know.
• Say: Diganxotte hillandi ke ko din n batten ŋa ( baaba) ma  an da /a/ sigire ke sehexanne mugu 
ya digaxotte (baaba) ke noxondi ya ba? An da mugu taanu manime ?
• Say: Sasa an an ta ni nan diganxotte ke ko. xa gana a konno, xa da xa kittun dorome taagu( a) 
xotte ke wure. Waxatin be, xa gada /a/ sehexanne ke ko.  
Hear and see the long vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture in the next row on the Pupil Book page.
• Say: Sere suu xawa ni  kitten dorome taaxundi naatali ke toxo ke wure a wuredan ŋa.
• Say: An da mani wari? Ken ni "a "
• Clap the syllables with the pupils.
• Say: /a/ sehexanne ken ka rawayi huutini. Ken wure ni o ga na a ko, o na huutunu nan a ña hoo 
gillen ŋa. Ma an da sigire gille ke sehexanne/ aa/ ke mugu wa ba diganxotte ke di.
• Write the word on the chalk board. Point to the long vowel. Ask pupils to point to the same 
vowel in their book. Ask pupils how many of the letters of the day they see next to each other. 
Answer: two
• Tell pupils that when they see two /a/ together, it makes a long sound /aa/. The long sound 
means that you stretch the sound longer when you say it.
• Demonstrate saying the short vowel sound and then the long vowel sound. Ask pupils to repeat. 
• Ensure that they can hear the difference between the short sound and the long (stretched) 
sound.
• Continue in the same way using the next picture. Look at it, say the word, clap the syllables and 
listen for the long vowel in the word.

activities.title: Writing – Letter
activities.content:
Write the letter and say its sound
• Write the letter /a/ on the board (1/3 meter tall).
• Air write the letter (use a straight arm), and say its sound as you write. Pupils should then try it 
two more times while you watch and provide feedback.
• Demonstrate writing the letter on the chalkboard once more.
• Ask pupils to take out their exercise books and write the letter 5 times

activities.title: Read aloud
activities.content:
• Read the following story aloud (use the appropriate big book or supplementary illustrations if 
available)
• During reading, stop to discuss people and places
• Pause at 2-3 pictures throughout the book while reading. Ask pupils, based on the pictures, 
where they think the story takes place. Ask pupils, based on the pictures, what the characters 
like to do. Assure pupil responses are related to the pictures.
• Possible questions (use these, or ask your own questions):
• Where do you think they are? How do you know? What more can you say about that place?
• Who do you think this person is? What is he/she doing? 
• Talk about how the picture relates to parts of the story you are reading aloud.

activities.title: Vocabulary – after reading
activities.content:
Check for vocabulary understanding
• Ask pupils if they heard the new vocabulary words during the read aloud.
• Call on 3 pupils at random to say what vocabulary word they heard and to say the meaning in 
their own words. Ask pupils how the word was used in the story.
• Say: diganta gurunbo saha ti o ga da diganxannu beenu xara.
• Give an example by using one of the words in a new sentence - one that is not in the pupil book 
or read aloud.
• For each other vocabulary word introduced before reading, ask a pupil to use the word in a new 
sentence. Have pupils act out a word, if appropriate. Congratulate, help, or correct the pupils, 
depending on the responses.

Then try again with the same student to be sure he or she knows the word.

activities.title: Comprehension questions— factual
activities.content:
Check for vocabulary understanding
• Review the question word "Minna" ("Where") 
• Read the question: 
• Where did Issah Live? Isa taaxunten na minna?  
• Answer: (Issah lived in a big forest). isa taaxunten wa diga xooren di.
• Ask pupils to answer the question. Give them feedback. 
• Say: ma xa da duuran diganxotten mugu ba o ga demi kubeenu tirindi koota danginton di.
• Ask pupils if they can tell you what the question word "where" is asking about. Call on one or 
two pupils to respond. Let them know if they are correct, or incorrect and why. (Response: the 
question word "where" asks us about a place)
• Teach pupils to use the question word "when" ("kan bire") 
• Tell pupils that they will learn a new question word today, "when". Tell pupils that they will use 
it to answer the next question.
• Read the question: "When do you like to play outside? Say: Kan bire ni an ga lahini telle sanga 
sella ŋa
• Call on 2 pupils to answer. Their answer should be a time (i.e. in the morning, after school, on 
the weekend)

• Say: digankontonte "kan bire"o na a ñaana na haqatin ya tirindi.n ga na a mugu, "kan bire" n 
na a tuunu ya nan ti jaabinde ke ni haqatin ya yi.a rawayi ñaana koota haqatin ŋa( xo soxoba), 
koyen koota(xo juma)ma siinen haqqati (xo xaaxo).
• Read the question: When does Issah want the workers to help him on his farm? Kan bire Isa 
gal ahi goŋñaŋaanun na I deema I tendi.
• Answer: Say: Isa lahi goliñaŋaanon na i deema xumbane . 
• Ask pupils to think about when, or the time, that this happened. 
• Call on pupils at random to respond.
• Read the question: Kon da i marahan ñoomi goppe  yi  
• Answer: Xñaanan yan da I marahan ñoomi goppe ke yi.
• Turn and Talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to talk about their answers to the 
question. 
• Call on a pupil to share their answer. Ask the rest of the class if they agree.

• Write the two sight words ( Aba and Fatou ) on the top of the board.

• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).

activities.title: Short and long vowel sound

Hear and see the short vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture on the page of the Pupil Book.

understand the word by saying it in another language they know.
• Say: O na soxo na gudan ku jonkoyi me. /si/ An da /i/ sehexanne mugu taanu mani me 
diganxanne ke di sirime.
• Touch the letter in the Pupil Book. Say the sound. If pupils struggle to hear and say the sound, 
help them by saying another word with that sound in your language or in another language 
they know.
• Say: Xa da diganxotte tana ko din batten ŋa. Diganxotte tana ke ni  /ide/. Xa da /i/ 
sehexanneh mugu wa ba diganxotte ke di?
• Say: Xa ya ta ni. Xa da diganxotte ke ko . An  gana konno , an kitten ñoomi /i/ sehexanne ke 
wure biran be an gada sehexanne ke ko.
• Hear and see the long vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture in the next row on the Pupil Book page.
• Say: Everyone should place their finger under the first picture at the bottom. What do you 
see? It is " ." Sere sun xawa I kitten doromen taxunu nataali hana ke wure. Xada mani wari? 
ke ni /kitte/
• Clap the syllables with the pupils.
• Say: /i/ sehexanne ke xa rawayi huutini. Ken wure ni o gana kono, o na huutunu na sehexanne 
gillen dabari. Ma xa da sigiri gillen ke / ii/ sehexanneh mugu wa ba diganxotte ke di /kiide/? 
• Write the word on the chalk board. Point to the long vowel. Ask pupils to point to the same 
vowel in their book. Ask pupils how many of the letters of the day they see next to each other. 
(Answer: two)
• Tell pupils that when they see two "o" together, it makes a long sound /oo/. The long sound 
means that you stretch the sound longer when you say it.
• Demonstrate saying the short vowel sound and then the long vowel sound. Ask pupils to 
repeat. 
• Ensure that they can hear the difference between the short sound and the long (stretched) 
sound.
• Continue in the same way using the next picture. Look at it, say the word, clap the syllables 
and listen for the long vowel in the word.

2. Comprehension questions- factual (10 mins)

• Read the first question: 
• Where was the goat acting ?  Sugo ke ñi minna yi? "  Answer: (The goat was acting silly in the 
house) sugu ke ñi kompen ya di
• Ask pupils to answer the question. Give them feedback. 
• Ask pupils if they can tell you what the question word "where" is asking about. Call on one or 
two pupils to respond. Let them know if they are correct, or incorrect and why. (Response: the 
question word "where" asks us about a place)
Teach pupils to use the question word "what" ("Mani") 
• Read the question: 
• Which fruit do you like the most?" 
• Call on 2-3 pupils at random to answer.
• Tell pupils that they will learn a new question word today, "what." Tell pupils that they will 
use it to answer the next question.
• Say: Diganqanne ke be ga ni "Mani" Ken ya na kono o da simmayen tana. ŋa na mugu "mani", 
Na tuunu nan ti yaabin de ke ñaana ho haayi kebe o ga walla, malla na katta yi.
• Say: Gellin in ga na  daaba kurumban ŋari, na tirindindin, "ke ni mani ya?" N lahi daaba ke 
toxon tuunu. Gelli ŋana  tirindindin," Mani"? N lahi hon tunu misaale ke gada hibe dabari.
• Read the question: 
• What is Komba's mum doing? Kumba ma wa mani daba riini? Answer: (Komba's mum was busy  
pounding fufu) Kumba maa ñi yillen ña gollo.
• Say: On simme o gada hibe xara. Gumanŋe ke ti : A ma kitten laganten ña ñi golle ke di, walla a 
ñi yilli golle ya."
• Ask pupils to think about what, or the thing, they are asking about. 
• Call on pupils at random to respond.
• Read the question: 
• What did the goat chew? Sugo ke da mani kambu?
• Answer: Sugo ke da yiraamu ña kanbu.
• Turn and Talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to talk about their answers to the 
question. Remind pupils that it is a "what" question.
• Call on a pupil to share their answer. Ask the rest of the class if they agree.

activities.title: Short and long vowel sound
activities.content:
• Hear and see the short vowel within a word

• Point to the first picture on the page of the Pupil Book.
• Say: An da mani wari ?
• Ask one pupil to name what is in the picture. Repeat the correct word. If needed, help pupils 
understand the word by saying it in another language they know.
• Say: On na o kittun wutu nan sooxo gudanu ku dan¿ani do / ro /ke An da /o/ sehexannen muxu 
taanu minna diganxotten noxondi (doroke)? On sooxo gudanun ku da xadi.
• Touch the letter in the Pupil Book. Say the sound. If pupils struggle to hear and say the sound, 
help them by saying another word with that sound in your language or in another language they 
know.
• Say:  Xa da diganxotte tana ko din batten ŋa. Xa da /o/ sehexanneh mugu wa ba diganxotte ke 
di?
• Hear and see the long vowel within a word
• Point to the first picture in the next row on the Pupil Book page.
• Say: O suu xawa o kittun doromu taaxunu nataali hana ke wure. Wureda.  Xa da mani wari? Ke 
ni (bido)
• Clap the syllables with the pupils.
• Say: /o/ sehexanne ke xa rawayi huutini. Ken wure ni o gana kono, o na huutunu na sehexanne 
gillen dabari. Ma xa da sigiri gillen /ii/ ke sehexanneh mugu wa ba (xooda) noxondi?
• Write the word on the chalk board. Point to the long vowel. Ask pupils to point to the same 
vowel in their book. Ask pupils how many of the letters of the day they see next to each other. 
Answer: two
• Tell pupils that when they see two "i" together, it makes a long sound /ii/. The long sound 
means that you stretch the sound longer when you say it.
• Demonstrate saying the short vowel sound and then the long vowel sound. Ask pupils to repeat. 
• Ensure that they can hear the difference between the short sound and the long (stretched) 
sound.
• Continue in the same way using the next picture. Look at it, say the word, clap the syllables and 
listen for the long vowel in the word.

Clap words with different numbers of syllables

syllables. Each syllable has a sound pattern. I am going to give two examples. Watch carefully. 
Let's clap our hands and see."
• Say: Siine ke jopandiranŋa O da xara nan ti an lawayi diganxottu  taxadini  gudanu ŋa. Guda

(without the teacher).

•  Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to begin reading the story in their Pupil Books.

should choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice for the story.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit with you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more pupils starting 
with the next pupil on the list.
• Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general sense 
of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may indicate that the child 
is struggling. 
• Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A total of 40-50 is 
good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider reinforcement activities for 
skill areas that are less than 40.
• Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list.
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning of the 
list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
Choose a reinforcement activity from the options 
below. Base your choice on the skill(s) your pupils 
found challenging in the assessment. The skill 
reinforced by the activity is in the activity name: 
"letter sounds" or "syllable blending".
• Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a pupil to say 
the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound.Ask pupils to think of a word that starts with 
the sound. Calls on5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next letter.
• Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly 
tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already 
learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate as 
possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
• Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to 
use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say its 
sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask 
pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the who flashcards. When they 
agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised 
their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of 
appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs
• Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllableson the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. Call 
one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote down 
raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation from the 
class.

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to put their fingers under the first word in the word list for the activity in the pupil 
book. Read the first word.
• Say: What is the meaning of this word? 
• Say: Ke diganxotte wure ni mani ya?
• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point to the picture on 
the page that matches that word.Ask all pupils to point to the next word in the list and whisper 
read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random to read the word for the class. Ask all pupils to 
point to the picture that matches the word.
• Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.

activities.title: Word building
activities.content:
Use syllables to build given words
• Tell pupils they will write words using the syllables in the box. 
• Say: I am thinking of a word. The word is: "beebe". Let us clap together "bee/be". Npay diganxotte 
yogo simmana,  Diganxotte ke ni /beebe/ o sun sooxo doome./bee/be/
• Ask pupils to point to the first syllable in the word on the Lesson 20 page in their Pupil Books. 
Then, write the syllable on the board.
• Continue asking pupils to point to the syllables in the word until the full word is written on the 
board.
• Say: The word is "beebe". Now we are done writing all the words. Let us read together.  Diganxotte 
ke ni beebe ya yi . Sasa o duguta diganxottu ku su sahana. O na a xara doome (Pupils read the 
word)
• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find the syllables of 
the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form the word in their copy books. 
After all pupils have written the word, say the next word. Continue with the rest of the words.
• Words: Enter words that can be made by syllables in the Pupil Book
•  beebe, beebi, baaba, baaba,
• Use syllables to build new words
• Say: Now, I want you to try if you can form your own words!
• Say: Sasa n lahi xa na diganqote dabarinde seera xa du da.
• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that they know and 
write it in their copy books.
• When pupils are finished, ask them to turn to a partner to share the word they made.

4. Read words (10 mins)

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit with you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more pupils 
starting with the next pupil on the list.
Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general sense 
of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may indicate that the 
child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A total of 40-50 
is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider reinforcement activities 
for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list.
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning of the 
list.

pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly tap the 
letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already learned. 
*TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate as possible, 
then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly.
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to use 
letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say its sound. 
Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask pupils to 
turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the who flashcards. When they agree on 
the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised their hands. 
Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of appreciation. 
Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. Call one 
of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote down raises 
their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation from the class.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit with you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more pupils 
starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).
Score the assessment - for each pupil

• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general sense 
of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may indicate that the 
child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A total of 40-50 
is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider reinforcement activities 
for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning of the 
list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE

assessment. The skill reinforced by the activity 
is in the activity name: "letter sounds" or 
"syllable blending". 
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a pupil to say 
the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a word that starts 
with the sound. Calls on5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly 
tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already 
learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate as 
possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to 
use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say its 
sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask 
pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the who flashcards. When they 
agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised 
their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of 
appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the items aloud 

once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. Call 
one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote down 
raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation from the 
class.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit with 
you.

• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10).Next week you will assess 10 more pupils 
starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).

Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general 
sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may indicate 
that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A total of 
40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider reinforcement 
activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning of the 
list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE

below. Base your choice on the skill(s) your 
pupils found challenging in the assessment. The 
skill reinforced by the activity is in the activity 
name: "letter sounds" or "syllable blending".
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a pupil to say 
the letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a word that starts 
with the sound. Calls on5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly 
tap the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already 
learned. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate as 
possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to 
use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say its 
sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask 
pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the who flashcards. When they 
agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised 
their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of 
appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. Call 
one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote down 
raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation from the 
class.

syllables independently again from their books.

activities.content:
Prepare for the assessment

Think about why you want to read the story

pupils.
• Say: O da yaxan nen wari siwo wa a yinben di o lah a tu nu a wa gilli mina. O na xara o na a tu. 
• Turn and talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to begin reading the story in their 
Pupil Books.
• Tell pupils that they will see a few words in the story missing. With their partners, they should 
choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice for the story.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit with 
you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10).Next week you will assess 10 more pupils 
starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).
Score the assessment - for each pupil

• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general 
sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may indicate 
that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A total of 
40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider reinforcement 
activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning of the 
list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
• Choose a reinforcement activity from the 
options below. Base your choice on the 
skill(s) your pupils found challenging in the 
assessment. The skill reinforced by the activity 
is in the activity name: "letter sounds" or 
"syllable blending".
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learned but need to practice. Ask a pupil to say the 
letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound.Ask pupils to think of a word that starts with the 
sound. Calls on5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound that 
pupils have already learned. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly tap the 
letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already learned. 
*TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate as possible, 
then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to use 
letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say its sound. 
Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask pupils to 
turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the flashcards. When they agree on the 
syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised their hands. Call 
on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of appreciation. Continue 
using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learned. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. Call one 
of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote down raises 
their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation from the class.

doome.''

their copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next word. Continue with

daba riini!''Saasa, ň lahi xa na xa duura diganxannun dabari!
• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that they 
know and write it in their copy books.

the word they made.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment

• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).

starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).

Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general 
sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may indicate 
that the child is struggling.

• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A total of 
40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider reinforcement 
activities for skill areas that are less than 40.

Letter sounds - Letter zoom

that pupils have already learnt. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly tap 
the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already 
learnt. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate as 
possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to 
use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say its 
sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask 
pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the who flashcards. When they 
agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised 
their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of 
appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learnt. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. Call 
one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote down 
raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation from the 
class.

activities.content:
Teach the letter
• Point to the small letter "j"on the alphabet poster or on the board.
• Say: ke y ani o sigiri Kurumba ke yi lenki. Ke xotte sehexannen ni / p/ O na a ko doome.
• Ask pupils to say the sound with you (no more than 2 times).
• Point to the capital letter "J" on the alphabet poster or on the board again.
• Say: Waxati gabe,o wa walla ke moxodi diganxannen di. 
Keyword picture study
• Say: An da mani wari?
• Call on 1-2 pupils to name what they see in the picture.
• Say the keyword. Touch the letter of the day in the keyword in the pupil book. Say the sound. 
• Say: O na diganxannen ke ko doome: /papa/ An na /p / sehexannen mukku / papa/ 
diganxanne ke di ya ba ?
• Ask pupils to touch the letter and say the word again.
Keyword analysis (Pupil Book Box #1)
• Write the keyword from Box #1 on the board. 
• Point to the keyword.
• Say: The word is  /jaba /.
• Say: Diganxanne ke ni /jaba /
• Point to the syllable (under the keyword). Read it and show pupils how the syllable is part of 
the keyword.
• Point to the letter (under the syllable). Read it and show pupils how the letter is part of the 
syllable.

activities.title: Read syllables
activities.content:
Use the new letter sound to read syllables (Pupil Book Box #2)
• Write the Box #2 syllable column on the board. 
• Point to the first syllable. Cover the "a" and show the "j".
• Say: Which sound is this? (pupils respond "…j..")  Kan sehexanne ni ke yi?

• Cover the "p" and show the "a".
• Say: Which sound is this? (pupils respond "a"). Kan sehexanne ni ke yi?
• Say: An lawayi gudan xarana na sehexannu ku kahuma me yi :  /p / / a/
• Continue in this way for the other syllables. Ask pupils to do the others. They will say each 
sound, and then the syllable. 
• After the pupils have read all the syllables together, give them 1 minute to try reading the 
syllables independently again from their books.
Rapid syllable reading (Pupil Book Box #3)
• Write the first column of Box #3 on the board.
• Ask pupils, all together, to read down the column on the board. 
• Write each additional column, one at a time. Have pupils read the syllables in each column.
• Point to 5 syllables randomly. Ask the whole class to read each one quickly as you point to it.

activities.title: Read words
activities.content:
Blending syllables to read words
• Write the first word on the chalkboard and help pupils find it in their books.
• Say: Terinka siri an na a haayi. N wa gudan xarana na gudanu ku kahuma me yi na 
diganxannen dabari.
• Model the blending process by reading each syllable, then blending the syllables together to 
read the word.
• Say: "Let us practice it and see."  ''O na seera.''
• Read the same syllables and the word, but this time with the pupils. Then ask the pupils to try 
the same word by themselves.
• Say: Saasa an da a tu an gan xawa hiibe Ñaana. Diganxanne ke xara an bukkin di moxo baane 
ke di. Guda ke xara hina, an na diganxanne ke ko.An ŋa na yi xarana, an kitti doromen Ñoomi 
do a batten ŋa.   (Monitor and help pupils.)
• Call on 4 pupils at random to read one of the words using the blending process - reading the 
syllables, then the word. Provide help if needed.

activities.content:

the Pupil's Book.

diganxotten terinkana,walla digantaanu o 
xannen di, luwanu do killu ñana no o gan xawa 
a walla do kebe yi.   
Ku luwanu do killu kuno o deema nan kattu hon fahamunu siri gelli o ku ,walla seren tana ŋana yi 
hokono o da.lenki, xoro na terenke kata hi kuruba baane yi.  
• Say: What do you see in the picture? O da mani wari natali ke di
• Say: Npayi riini diganxotten ko walla na diganta xara. Xa terenke moxo siri.[…………….]

• Say: Xa da mani haamu diganxottu do diganta?    
• Answer: ku Diganxnanu hilli digamunu hiinu dingiranu  kanma .Diganxanne hana ke ti hibe ga 
a kanma ,diganxanne hillandi ke ti a wa  a wure dan ŋa

• Call 1-2 learners to give similar example of my language rule and explain what it means.

activities.content:
Teach and discuss vocabulary

each one.
• Discuss the word meaning, using gestures or illustrations to support understanding. If 
needed, help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language they know.

activities.title: Comprehension - Prediction
activities.content:
Teach the letter

• Help pupils find the decodable text of the day in their Pupil Books by holding up the page and 
saying the page number.
• Say: Ke natali haayi. An da mani wari? An da mani sinma ke gumaane Ñaana mani kanma?
• Give pupils a moment to think, then invite them to share their predictions with a partner. Call 
on 2 pupils at random and ask for their predictions.

activities.title: Reason to read
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story
• Say: Saasa an baane na gumanŋe ke xara an bukkin di. An na diganxannu ku xara gumanŋen 
noxondi bawoni i sahanten na o da diganxannu beenu xara.
• Say: O da yugon ŋari a wa taagunu deddin xaaran ŋa. O na a xara na tu a wa mani ñana non 
ŋa. 
• Say: An du naha ti xottun do sehexannu beenu an gada i tu nan katu gumanŋe ke xarana an 
duda. Diganxane su Ñoomi ti an doronmen ŋa haxati su.

activities.title: Decodable story reading – Independent
activities.content:
Pupils read aloud in the book independently
• Ask pupils to read the decodable story independently. They should whisper read (read 
quietly), putting their finger under each word as they read it. If pupils finish reading early, 
they can read the story again with a partner.
• Walk around the classroom while pupils read. Help pupils use the skills they have learnt to 
read words. They should blend sounds to read syllables, and blend syllables to read words.

activities.title: Comprehension – Prediction check
activities.content:
Check prediction based on picture
• Ask pupils to remember their predictions from before they read the story. Give them a moment 
to think. Ask them to raise their hands if their predictions were what happened in the story.
• Remind the class what the volunteer pupils predicted before they read the story. Ask the 
pupils if those predictions were what happened.

activities.title: Writing – Letters
activities.content:
Pupils practice writing the letter
• Ask pupils to locate the letter "j" in a word in the decodable story. Call on 2 pupils at random 
to share the words they found.
• Write the letter "j"on the board (1/3 meter tall).
• Air write the letter (use a straight arm) and describe how to write the letter as you do it. 
Invite pupils to air write with you and say the sound. Watch them as they do it.
• Ask pupils to write the letter with a finger on their desks while saying the sound of the letter.
• Ask pupils to take out their exercise books and write the letter "j"5 times.
• If some pupils finish early, tell them to draw a picture of something that begins with the sound 
/j/.

jojjo jame daga jaba jaaguye

activities.title: Comprehension – making connections
activities.content:
Ask comprehension questions
• Call on a pupil randomly to answer the following question:
• Question 1: Wulle ke da I menjaŋen Ña kanmoxo? (Jaabinde: A da toxo geden di).  

• Question 2: Sugo ke da I menjanŋen Ña kanmoxo?  (Jaabinde: A da killen ya koyi na a deema 
nan sege.) 
• After each question, call on a pupil randomly to share their answer to the question. Discuss 
their answers with the class. Help the pupils think about what is in the text or picture, as well 
as their own experiences, to reflect on what may have given them that idea.
• Make text-to-self connections
• Say: Saasa, sinme xo Wulle ke gada Sugo ke Ña moxobe. O nan xawa o menjanŋun ragana ti I 
moxon ŋa kan moxo ya di?
• Ask pupils to turn to a partner to share their answers.
• Call on a pupil randomly to share their answer to the question. Discuss their answer with the 
class. Help the pupils think about how the story relates to their own lives and how they can 
use their own experiences to understand the story.

activities.title: Assessment: BEFORE THE LESSON
activities.content:
Prepare for the assessment
• Prepare an assessment page in a notebook. 
List all the pupils in the class in alphabetical 
order. Then make 3 more columns with the title 
"letters", "syllables" and "individual score".
• At the beginning of this lesson, help pupils find 
the decodable story for this lesson. Instruct 
pupils who are not being assessed to read the 
story quietly.

activities.title: Reason to Read
activities.content:
Think about why you want to read the story
• Tell pupils that they will be reading a story with a partner while you work with individual 
pupils.
• Say: O da gaaja do gane ŋari han laxen ŋa o lahi a tuunu I daga mani ya  non ŋa. O na a xara 
na tu.
• Turn and talk: Ask pupils to turn to a pupil next to them to begin reading the story in their 
Pupil Books.
• Tell pupils that they will see a few words in the story missing. With their partners, they should 
choose which of the two options in parenthesis is the correct choice for the story.

activities.title: Assessment (individual assessment while the rest of the class reads in pairs)
activities.content:
Administer the assessment
• You will assess 10 pupils. While the whole class is reading in pairs, call one pupil to sit with 
you.
• Open the assessment booklet to the assessment for this week. 
• Show the pupil the 5 letters. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Show the pupil the 5 syllables. Mark the number of correct responses (from 1-5).
• Do this for another 9 pupils (to complete all 10). Next week you will assess 10 more pupils 
starting with the next pupil on the list (pupil # 11).

Score the assessment - for each pupil
• Total the correct letters and syllables for each pupil - across the row. This gives a general 
sense of how the child is learning: 8-10 correct is good. 6-7 is developing. 1-5 may indicate 
that the child is struggling. 
Score the assessment - for class progress
• Total the correct letters and syllables for the 10 pupils by adding each column. A total of 
40-50 is good, 30-40 is developing, and less than 30 is a challenge. Consider reinforcement 
activities for skill areas that are less than 40.
Looking forward
• Next week, continue with the next 10 pupils on the list (pupils #11-20).
• Continue this way until all pupils are assessed, then start over again from the beginning of the 
list.

activities.title: Reinforcement activities
activities.content:
NOTE
• Choose a reinforcement activity from the 
options below. Base your choice on the 
skill(s) your pupils found challenging in the 
assessment. The skill reinforced by the activity 
is in the activity name: "letter sounds" or 
"syllable blending".
Letter sounds - Can you think of a word?
• Use flashcards. Hold up a letter pupils have learnt but need to practice. Ask a pupil to say the 
letter sound. Repeat the correct letter sound. Ask pupils to think of a word that starts with 
the sound. Calls on 5-10 pupils to share their words, then move on to the next letter.
Letter sounds - Letter zoom
• Ask pupils to turn to the table of letters at the back of the pupil book. Call a letter sound 
that pupils have already learnt. Ask pupils to look at the letters in the table and quickly tap 
the letter that makes that sound. Repeat with additional letters that pupils have already 
learnt. *TIP - start saying letter sounds at a speed that gets as many pupils to participate as 
possible, then gradually start saying letter sounds more quickly. 
Syllable blending - Whisper the syllable
• Use flashcards. Choose 3 consonants and 3 short or long vowels from the flashcards (try to 
use letters that pupils may struggle with or have forgotten). Hold up a consonant and say its 
sound. Hold up a short or long vowel and say its sound (or have pupils say the sound). Ask 
pupils to turn to a partner and quietly say the syllable made by the two flashcards. When they 
agree on the syllable, have them raise their hands. Wait until most of the class has raised 
their hands. Call on a pair at random to say the syllable. If they are correct, give a clap of 
appreciation. Continue using flashcards to make 5-10 more syllables for pupils to say in pairs. 
Syllable blending - Phonics bingo
• Write 10 syllables on the blackboard that pupils have already learnt. Read the items aloud 
once. Ask pupils to choose 3 of them to write in a notebook, paper, slate, or other place. Call 
one of the syllables at random. The first pupil to hear all 3 of the syllables they wrote down 
raises their hand. If they can say all 3 correct items, they get a clap of appreciation from the 
class.

activities.title: Word matching
activities.content:
• Ask pupils to put their fingers under the first word in the word list for the activity in the pupil 
book. Read the first word.
• Say: Ke diganxanne wure ni mani ya? 
• Ask for a volunteer to tell say the meaning of the word. Then, ask pupils to point to the picture 
on the page that matches that word.Ask all pupils to point to the next word in the list and 
whisper read it to themselves. Call on a pupil at random to read the word for the class. Ask all 
pupils to point to the picture that matches the word.
• Continue the activity to the end of the word list, helping pupils that get stuck.

activities.title: Word building
activities.content:
Use syllables to build given words
• Tell pupils they will write words using the syllables in the box. 
• Say: "I am thinking about a word. The word is '……jaaba….' Let's break it down and clap it out 
in syllables: /…../…../."
• Say: N haayi sinmene diganxannen ŋa. Diganxannen ke ni' /jaaba/ .' O na a taxandi na gudanu 
ku sooxo: /ja/…../ba
• Ask pupils to point to the first syllable in the word on the Lesson 20 page in their Pupil Books. 
Then, write the syllable on the board.
• Continue asking pupils to point to the syllables in the word until the full word is written on the 
board.
• Say: Diganxanne ke ni 'pono' Saasa o da diganxanne ke su saha. O na a xara doome. (Pupils 
read the word)
• Say the first word below and clap the syllables with pupils. Give pupils time to find the 
syllables of the word and point to them in their book, then write them to form the word in 
their copy books. After all pupils have written the word, say the next word. Continue with the 
rest of the words.
• Words: jaaba/  /jaba / jaajei/ caabi /habbi/
• Use syllables to build new words
• Say: Saasa, N lahi an na haayi ma an lawayi an duran diganxannun sahana 
• Ask pupils to use any of the syllables in the pupil book to make another word that they know 
and write it in their copy books.
• Turn and talk: When pupils are finished, ask them to turn to a pupil next to them to share the 
word they made.
